items.note: Walksnail's own product page states the output levels in milliwatts in the feature copy - 'switches between 25mW and 100mW output' - and prints no EIRP row at all, so there is nothing for this figure to contradict. Output power, the same quantity as the analog listings in this column. The retail listing is a second source for the power figure and agrees: it prints 'Transmit Power (EIRP): <20dBm', and 20 dBm is 100 mW - an EIRP ceiling that matches the manufacturer's stated 100 mW output rather than exceeding it. mount_mm is that listing's 'Mounting Hole: 25mm' line, read as the 25x25mm square those holes describe. It used to hold '14x15mm', which is two of the three figures in 'Camera: 12 x 14 x 15mm' - the camera's body, not the transmitter's holes.

max_power_mw and power_levels_mw are DJI's own figures from the O4 Air Unit Series user manual v1.0 (section 4.3 Setting Transmission Power, p17): 'DJI O4 Air Unit: The maximum available transmission power levels are 25mW, 50mW, 100mW, 200mW, 400mW, and 700mW.' These are output-power levels in milliwatts, the same quantity the analog listings in this column print, and NOT the Transmitter Power (EIRP) dBm figures DJI publishes elsewhere - EIRP includes antenna gain and is a different measurement. Available levels are lower in regions whose regulations cap them (DJI states this in the same block). weight_g is deliberately empty: the listing prints 'Air Unit (camera module excluded): Approx. 5.1 g', 'Air Unit (camera module included): Approx. 8.2 g' and 'Antenna: Approx. 0.75 g' under one 'Weight:' label, plus a sentence reading 'With the lens mount, the weight is 9.2 grams' - four figures for four things, and nothing says which one this column holds. The 9.2 g it used to show came from that sentence.

max_power_mw and power_levels_mw from DJI's O4 Air Unit Series user manual v1.0 (section 4.3, p17): 'DJI O4 Air Unit Pro: The maximum available transmission power levels are 25mW, 50mW, 100mW, 200mW, 400mW, 700mW, and 1200mW.' The same page adds that above 700mW the unit trims itself between the set value and 700mW based on the flight environment, so 1200 mW is the ceiling, not a sustained figure. Output power in milliwatts, not EIRP. mount_mm is the listing's own 'VTX Mounting Pattern: 20x20/25.5x25.5mm' line, which the scraper now reads in place of the '33.5x13mm' it used to take from 'Dimensions: 33.5 x 33.5 x 13 mm (L x W x H)'. weight_g is deliberately empty: the listing prints three weights under one 'Weight:' label - 'Air Unit (camera module excluded): Approx. 15.6 g', 'Air Unit (camera module included): Approx. 32 g' and 'Antenna: Approx. 2.1 g/pcs' - and nothing on the page says which of them is the figure this column holds, so it holds none of them. The 2.1 g it used to show was the antenna.

items.model: O4 Air Unit Pro Transmission Module
items.note: This SKU is the O4 Air Unit Pro's video transmission module sold without the camera - the retail listing gives 'Compatibility: DJI O4 Air Unit Pro' and sells it for repair and replacement - so it is the same radio as the kit and carries the kit's figures from DJI's O4 Air Unit Series user manual v1.0 (section 4.3, p17). Output power in milliwatts, not EIRP. mount_mm is the kit listing's 'VTX Mounting Pattern: 20x20/25.5x25.5mm' line: this SKU is that kit's transmission module, so it is the same board with the same holes, and its own listing states no pattern at all. What it used to hold was '33.5x13mm', two of the three figures the same listing prints as 'Dimensions: 33.5 x 33.5 x 13 mm (L x W x H)'.

Wideband version of the Reaper Extreme: 80 channels spread over 4.9-6.0 GHz instead of the 40-72 channels of the 5.8 GHz-only model. 36x27.5x8 mm CNC shell, 5 V BEC for the camera, built-in microphone, 1.2 A draw at 9 V. Retailer spec blocks disagree on the top step - some list 1.5 W as the maximum while the model is sold as 2.5 W; Foxeer's own manual gives the five steps recorded here.

The 10 W step of the Infinity line. Output at this level is far above what most countries allow unlicensed on 5.8 GHz - check local rules before transmitting. Weight is not published consistently across listings, so it is left out rather than guessed.
Long-range transmitter: 41x20x17 mm, 58 g including the heatsink, 5 V output for the camera. The V2 widens the original 5.8 GHz 40-channel model to 4.9-6.0 GHz and 80 channels.

Ukrainian-made transmitter, 96 channels across 12 bands covering 4867-5945 MHz. 53x28.85x16 mm with an aluminium heatsink and a cooling fan; controlled over IRC Tramp from the flight controller. FT Systems quotes measured RF output of 2200-5080 mW across the range rather than a single figure, because a wideband amplifier does not deliver the same power at every frequency - the 4000 mW here is the nominal setting.

items.note: Silkscreen on the SMA board: power steps PIT / 25 / 200 / 400 / 800 mW, band A with eight channels (1080, 1120, 1160, 1200, 1240, 1280, 1320, 1360 MHz), DC 7-30 V. Sold in an SMA and a U.FL version, so the connector column stays empty - it is a choice, not this board's socket. Output above the lowest step is licensed spectrum in most countries; the module's own label carries that reminder.

RushFPV calls this one the Tank Ultimate MINI2. Its spec block: 7-36 V DC in, 5 V 1 A out, 48 channels (37 on the US version), power PIT/25/200/500/800 mW, installation hole 20 x 20 mm, board 28 x 28 x 3.3 mm, and 'Weight: 4.46 g (without dust cover), 5.4 g (with dust cover)'. The 4.46 g this page shows is the first of those two; which of them the column should hold is the open question about a part weighed with and without an accessory, so the figure is left as it is and both are recorded here.

RushFPV's own spec block: 7-36 V DC in, 5 V/1 A (600 mA) out, 48 channels, power PIT/25/400/800/MAX mW, 37 x 24 x 6.7 mm, 12 g without cable - which confirms the 12 g and the 48 channels this page already carried. The top step is printed as 'MAX' with no figure, so power_levels records it as printed and max_power_mw keeps the 1000 mW the retail listing states.

RushFPV's own spec block for the Tiny Tank: 5 V input, 1.4 g, 48 channels (37 on the US version), U.FL, TBS Smart Audio, power PIT/25/100/200/MAX 350 mW - the only Tank whose top step is printed with its figure, which is where the 350 mW this page already carried is confirmed.

X-SPAN is RushFPV's name for its wideband analog module line - a standalone brick with an SMA jack, a fan and a dual DC-in that also feeds the camera, not a board you bolt into a stack.
